subsystem.name: GenericRuntimeObjects
subsystem.responsibility: Cross-cutting runtime services shared by the engine: COM-style pointer-to-pointer interface handles with single-slot vtable dispatch (slots 0x58/0x60/0x64), mutex-guarded singly-linked list containers with data-flag teardown, socket lifecycle management, network session command/protocol dispatch (UDP status replies, mutex-protected lobby-state word 1-5, direct-connect bind-port scan), config/command string parsing into a fixed output record, compiler-style guarded static initialization, and cleanup/free callback registration through BooleanToIntConversion.

summary: This packet spans nineteen functions that implement generic runtime plumbing rather than any single feature. A cluster of four functions (0x0057A680, 0x0057A690, 0x0057A6A0, 0x0057A730) operate through a COM-style handle: *this holds an interface object pointer, the vtable base is *obj, and a __thiscall method at a fixed slot (0x60, 0x64, or 0x58) is dispatched on obj. Four more functions (0x0057A950, 0x0057A990, 0x0057AA70, 0x0057AE80) are trivial wrappers that forward a cleanup/free routine's address to BooleanToIntConversion (0x00587B3E). 0x0057A980 is compiler-style once-guarded static initialization. A large server-side command dispatcher (0x0057BF00) handles prefix-checked network commands: UDP status replies built from getsockname data, a mutex-protected lobby-state word at this+0x5C4 (values 1-5) gated on this+0x5D and this+0x618 mutexes, and a direct-connect sequence with a bind-port scan retry loop and a peer node registered under the this+0xBEC mutex. Socket lifecycle (0x0057C8E0) and a config-string parser into a 5-byte record (0x0057CA10) are isolated helpers. Four list-teardown functions (0x0057E570, 0x0057E6E0, 0x0057E760, 0x0057E7E0) each destroy a mutex-protected singly-linked list, all invoked by NetworkCleanup_fbe0 (0x0057FBE0); they share the node shape {data@+0, next@+4, flag@+8} and free node data via FreeWrapper_7bcf when the flag byte is set. 0x005804A0 initializes a network listener (UDP bind at this+0x910, TCP bind at +50, vtable+72 init and vtable+144 post-listen callbacks). 0x00584230 is a 15-case session-protocol message dispatcher driven by a bitmask decoded from a packet entry table, and 0x00585040 drains a vtable-dispatched queue plus a mutex-guarded node list. Class ownership is uncertain (owner trust UNKNOWN throughout the packet); the class grouping below is DERIVED from shared this+0x offset usage, and must not be read as proven single-owner structures.

Server-side network command dispatch: one-time cache of prefix length into dword_8D3C14, prefix reject (return 0), bounded command-token split, then three branches: UDP status reply built from getsockname with reply-code lowered by this+0x5D; mutex-protected lobby-state write (1-5) at this+0x5C4 gated by this+0x618; and a direct-connect sequence (bind-port scan with WSAEADDRINUSE retry, peer registration under this+0xBEC, two notify rounds, teardown). Returns 1 on handled paths.

Graceful socket close: when the stored handle is not INVALID_SOCKET (-1), shutdown(SD_SEND) when the graceful flag is set, drain via recv until 0/-1, closesocket, write -1 back; return the closesocket result.

Parse a config/command string with two delimiter types into a 5-byte output record: primary delimiter byte_5C3F6C segments (bounded copies via sub_587DD0), secondary delimiter word_5BEB48 sub-segments converted to bytes via sub_587ECE; word result at a2+2, four bytes at a2+4..a2+7; return 1 on full success, 0 on any null segment.

Mutex-protected connection-list cleanup: acquire this+0xABC (timeout this+0xAC0), walk nodes until the shared head record, unlink, destroy via sub_491E40 and free via FreeWrapper_7bcf, reset head-record fields and ring buffer under the this+0xBEC handle, re-queue the record, release mutexes.

Mutex-protected linked-list teardown: acquire mutex at this+0xAD8 (timeout this+0xADC), walk nodes from this+0xAC8, call the first vtable entry (destructor, argument 1) on node data only when node+0x8 flag and node+0x0 data are set, free every node via FreeWrapper_7bcf, clear this+0xAC8..0xAD4, release mutex.

Mutex-protected singly-linked-list flush/destroy: wait on this+0xB10 (timeout this+0xB14), walk from this+0xB00 following node+0x4, free node data via FreeWrapper_7bcf when node+0x8 flag is set, free each node, zero this+0xB00..0xB0C, release this+0xB10 mutex.

Mutex-protected singly-linked-list destruction: wait on this+0xB2C (timeout this+0xB30), walk from this+0xB1C following node+0x4, free node data via FreeWrapper_7bcf when node+0x8 flag is set, free every node, zero this+0xB1C..0xB28, release this+0xB2C mutex.

Network listener initialization: vtable+72 init callback, thread resume (0x00585680), UDP bind at this+0x93C to base port this+0x910 and TCP bind at this+0x938 to base port+50, IP-string copy via sub_587DD0, config byte flags this+0x967..0x96B, then on success listen() with 0x7FFFFFFF backlog, ThreadSafeWriteWithMutex(4), vtable+144 post-listen callback, and MutexProtectedFieldWrite; returns 6 on bind failure.

Session-protocol message dispatcher: decode a bitmask of pending connection/handshake IDs from the packet entry table a2 (base a2[7]+4*a2[14], mask a2[5]) via IndexToBitmaskConversion (0x00585E80), then route one of 15 message types (connection request, ping/latency, HST/clock, node add/remove, data transfer, clock sync) through this-object vtable slots with mutex-guarded shared fields (this+0x5C4, this+0x618); unhandled masks return 0.

Drain two queues and release the owning mutex: pop a mutex-guarded queue via sub_584CD0 dispatching each value through vtable +0x5C, then drain a second linked list under mutex this+0x5A8 (unlink matching node, free data via SEHGuardedFunctionWithExceptionHandling and FreeWrapper_7bcf, free node), then ReleaseMutex.

classes.name: NetworkSessionListener
classes.responsibility: Owning object for server-side network session handling: command dispatch, listener initialization, session-protocol message dispatch, plus the sockets, mutexes, state word, flag bytes, and peer-node list referenced by those three methods. Class grouping is DERIVED from shared this+0x offsets; the packet never proves a single owner type.

classes.name: NetworkConnectionListOwner
classes.responsibility: Holds several mutex-guarded singly-linked lists with the shared node shape {data@+0, next@+4, flag@+8} and provides their teardown/cleanup. The four methods are grouped because they are all invoked by NetworkCleanup_fbe0 (0x0057FBE0) and share the same list-walk/free pattern; they operate on distinct offset blocks (0xAAC/0xAC8/0xB00/0xB1C) that may belong to one large struct or several objects.

classes.name: ComInterfaceHandle
classes.responsibility: Pointer-to-pointer COM-style handle object: *this holds an interface object pointer, the vtable base is loaded from *obj, and a fixed __thiscall slot (0x58, 0x60, or 0x64) is dispatched on obj. The dispatched method identities are unknown.

classes.name: CleanupCallbackRegistrar
classes.responsibility: Set of near-identical thunks that materialize the address of a cleanup/free routine (sub_57A960, sub_57A9A0, sub_57AA80, sub_57AE90) and forward it as an integer argument to BooleanToIntConversion (0x00587B3E), returning its result. Whether the helper dereferences/invokes the address or merely converts a numeric value is not established.

classes.name: GuardedStaticInitScope
classes.responsibility: Compiler-style once-guarded static initialization: registers an SEH frame, runs a one-time guard on a global init counter, and constructs six static objects linked into a parent frame. The constructed object identities are unresolved.

classes.name: SocketHandleLifecycle
classes.responsibility: Graceful closing of a socket handle stored at *a1: INVALID_SOCKET (-1) sentinel, optional shutdown(SD_SEND) + recv drain, closesocket, and write-back of -1. The owning module/object is unknown.

classes.name: ConfigCommandStringParser
classes.responsibility: Parses a configuration/command string using a primary byte delimiter and a secondary word delimiter into a 5-byte output record (word at a2+2, four bytes at a2+4..a2+7). The record layout and the consumer are unresolved; no callers appear in the packet.

classes.name: QueueDrainListOwner
classes.responsibility: Owning object for a vtable-dispatched queue and a mutex-guarded node list drained together during shutdown: pops values via sub_584CD0 dispatching through vtable slot +0x5C, then unlinks and frees matching nodes (payload freed via SEHGuardedFunctionWithExceptionHandling when the node+0x8 flag is set) under the this+0x5A8 mutex.

state_machines.name: SessionStateWord
transitions: state field this+0x5C4 written under the this+0x618 mutex with 2, 3, 4 or 5 selected by the parsed command length, default 1
direct-connect success advances the state via ThreadSafeWriteWithMutex(2)
listener init records state 4 via ThreadSafeWriteWithMutex(4)
server-state byte this+0x5D lowers the status reply code from 4 to 3 (reply code, distinct from the state word)

state_machines.name: SessionProtocolDispatchMask
transitions: decoded bitmask v46 (accumulated via IndexToBitmaskConversion over packet entry table) selects one case through jump table 0x00584C28
every handled case returns success flag 1; unhandled bitmask values return 0

interfaces.name: ComStyleInterfaceHandle
interfaces.purpose: Pointer-to-pointer COM-style handle used to dispatch fixed vtable slots (0x58, 0x60, 0x64) on an interface object; the concrete interface contracts are unknown.

interfaces.name: NetworkSessionListenerDispatchTable
interfaces.purpose: Vtable-slot interface exercised by the session listener methods: slot 0x58 (88) obtains the session object, slot 0x48 (72) is the init callback, slot 0x90 (144) is the post-listen callback; message cases route through many further slots on this-object vtables.

interfaces.name: QueueDispatchVTable
interfaces.purpose: Single vtable slot (+0x5C / 92) on the queue-drain owner through which each popped queue value is dispatched as (*(*this + 92))(this, value).

compatibility_contracts.name: ComStyleHandleDispatchContract
compatibility_contracts.description: A caller passes a pointer-to-pointer handle: *this holds the interface object, *obj holds the vtable base, and a __thiscall method at vtable slot 0x58/0x60/0x64 is invoked on obj with *this as the this pointer, returning the method's integer result. A replacement must reproduce the single-dereference handle layout and these slot conventions.

compatibility_contracts.name: MutexGuardedLinkedListNodeContract
compatibility_contracts.description: Mutex-guarded singly-linked lists expose nodes of shape {data@+0, next@+4, flag@+8}; teardown frees the node data via FreeWrapper_7bcf (0x00587BCF) only when the +8 flag byte is set, always frees the node, then zeroes the four list-head dwords (head/tail/cursor/count) and releases the mutex. A replacement list container must preserve this node layout and the data-ownership flag semantics.

compatibility_contracts.name: SocketGracefulCloseContract
compatibility_contracts.description: A socket handle stored at *a1 is closed gracefully: if it equals -1 (INVALID_SOCKET) nothing happens; otherwise when the graceful flag is set shutdown(SD_SEND) runs and inbound data is drained with recv(*a1, buf, 256, 0) until it returns 0 or -1, then closesocket(*a1) and the handle is written back as -1. The closesocket result is returned.

compatibility_contracts.name: NetworkCommandPrefixProtocol
compatibility_contracts.description: Incoming network commands must carry a prefix whose length is cached once into dword_8D3C14 (from off_5E537C); a string not starting with that prefix is rejected with return 0. The suffix (capped at 79) is split against follow-up prefixes off_5E5384/off_5E5388/off_5E538C selecting status-reply, state-change (lobby-state word 1-5 at this+0x5C4), or direct-connect handling. The reply code is lowered from 4 to 3 when the this+0x5D byte is non-zero. Direct-connect binds base port this+0x910 + offset (TCP +50) with WSAEADDRINUSE retry. Wire semantics are reconstructed only to DERIVED level.
